title: Orthogonality of monomials under limited independence
statement: Let $n,k\ge0$, let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, and let $A$ assign to each $\omega\in\Omega$ a sign vector in $\{-1,1\}^n$. For a subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, write $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}x_i$. Suppose the distribution of $A(\omega)$, with $\omega$ uniform on $\Omega$, has all nonconstant Fourier coefficients indexed by sets of size at most $k$ equal to zero. Then for any subsets $S,T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $|S\cup T|\le k$, the uniform expectation over $\omega\in\Omega$ of $\chi_S(A(\omega))\chi_T(A(\omega))$ is $1$ if $S=T$ and $0$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: The induced distribution has zero nonconstant Fourier coefficients on sets of size at most $k$
